verdicts.title: Self-referential dict.update obscures setting inline='always'
verdicts.reasoning: Checked proxy.py lines 48-49 directly. Line 48: `jit_opts = jit_options.copy()`. Line 49: `jit_opts.update(jit_opts, inline='always')`. Python's dict.update with a mapping as the first positional arg merges that mapping's items into self — when source and target are the same object, all key-value pairs already exist so the positional argument is a no-op. The only effective operation is the `inline='always'` keyword. Confirmed that `jit_opts` (with inline) is used at line 69 in the exec'd template (`@njit(sig, **jit_opts)`) while `jit_options` (without inline) is used at line 53 for `func_jit`, so behavior is correct. The self-merge is genuinely dead effort; the intent is simply `jit_opts['inline'] = 'always'`. Low severity is appropriate — no correctness issue, purely a readability smell.
